```sql
WITH g AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)         AS q,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents) AS r,
           GROUPING(ol.order_id, pv.id) AS gid
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((pv.product_id, ol.order_id), (pv.product_id, pv.id))
),
a AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*)       FILTER (WHERE gid = 1)         AS order_count,
           (sum(q)        FILTER (WHERE gid = 1))::bigint AS quantity,
           sum(r)         FILTER (WHERE gid = 1)         AS revenue_cents,
           count(*)       FILTER (WHERE gid = 2)         AS variant_count
      FROM g
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       a.variant_count
  FROM a
  JOIN products p ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De twee `count(DISTINCT …)` dwongen een grote sortering op `(p.id, o.id)` af, die naar schijf spilde. Die vervang ik door één gehashte `GROUPING SETS`-aggregatie: per (product, order) en per (product, variant). Het tellen van die groepen geeft exact dezelfde distinct-aantallen, en de cast naar `bigint` op `quantity` behoudt het oorspronkelijke kolomtype. Daarnaast worden de brede `products`-kolommen pas na de aggregatie gejoind, alleen voor de ongeveer 1.750 resterende producten.
